cues.text: Expansion decisions usually live in slides, spreadsheets, email and task tools.
Numbers drift, approvals get lost, and no one can say what was agreed.
Market Expansion keeps one case per decision — here ME-104, German food-processing plants.
Evidence, sizing, validation, approvals, pilot and outcome stay together, with an owner and a stage.
Every number says what kind of claim it is.
Evidence is sourced. An assumption has an owner. A scenario is calculated. An actual is measured.
An AI draft stays a draft until a person accepts it.
TAM: 5,000 sites, €100m/year. SAM: 2,000 unique sites, €40m/year.
Reachable pool: 500 unique sites. SOM, a year-3 scenario: €2.0m annual revenue.
Each rung answers a different question. They are never added up.
Four gates: G0 scope, G1 validate, G2 pilot, G3 scale.
A person with authority decides — for example “Approve pilot €120k · 90 days” — on the exact snapshot they read.
If the case changes, the snapshot goes stale and is decided again. Nothing passes a gate on its own.
An approved pilot becomes owned tasks sent to your task tool.
A task shows “Confirmed · PIL-11” only after Jira returns the key. Failed tasks retry without duplicates.
Finishing tasks never passes a gate.
At the review, actuals are compared with thresholds set before the pilot.
A negative result is still a result: “Revise and extend validation”, with its own cap, €30k · 45 days.
G3 Scale stays blocked until its own preconditions are met.
Illustrative data: Aster Industrial Systems and its people are fictional.

roleLines.build: You build the case: shortlist, size, validate, then submit G2 for a decision.
roleLines.decide: You decide within your authority: read the package, then choose a scoped action. Nothing is approved until you do.
roleLines.run: You run the pilot: your tasks, the plan, and what reached Jira.
roleLines.review: You review what you are asked to: confirm, dispute or abstain, always with a reason.
roleLines.configure: You set up connections, roles and policies. Administrators configure; they never approve.
